memory.note: Verified 2026-09-05 on this machine: `claude --help` lists `--add-dir <directories...>`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--model` and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; ~/.claude/projects/ held 48 project directories with a memory/ subdirectory, keyed by the absolute cwd with every / and . replaced by -.

ready.note: TM-151, measured 2026-09-09 on live panes with `tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{C/r:<pattern>}'`, which answers the first matching line number or 0. A READY Claude composer does not always render an empty box: on a session with no history it renders the placeholder hint, `❯ Try "fix lint errors"` or `❯ Try "create a util logging.py that..."`. The old pattern forbade letters after the glyph, so it answered 0 on both of those live panes while the candidate answered 12. That is not a slow launch, it is a launch that never happens: readiness failing means the role session is never REGISTERED, so `role status reviewer` reads registered:false and every governed launch refuses with TOPOLOGY_STARTUP_NOT_READY. The hint branch is deliberately literal — `Try "` and nothing looser — because widening it to 'letters are allowed' would readmit the case ready.pattern exists to reject: an agent mid-answer with its own text on the line.

composer.note:
Measured 2026-09-09 against tmux 3.4 with `tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{C/r:<pattern>}'`, which answers the matching line number or 0. Live idle pane %4 (Claude Code, an empty input box rendering ❯ followed by U+00A0 and nothing else) answered 17; a second idle pane answered 54, and a bare shell answered 1. The negative is what makes it a COMPOSER test rather than a prompt test: a pane rendering `❯ read the inbox file 001-ping` answers 0, because `[^a-zA-Z0-9]*$` forbids letters or digits after the glyph. It also answers 0 on the plan-approval modal (pane %15, which draws `❯ 1. Yes, and switch to BYPASS PERMISSIONS`) — the TM-111 case where Enter means something destructive.

TM-151 added the placeholder-hint branch HERE TOO, and it is a separate decision from the ready one rather than a find-and-replace. The hint renders ONLY when the box is empty — it is placeholder text, which is exactly what this field asks about — so without the branch an empty composer showing a hint reads as NON-EMPTY, the delivery state machine calls a submitted message `typed-unsubmitted`, and rung R0 resubmits into a composer that already sent. The TM-111 negatives are preserved unchanged: `❯ No, exit` and `❯ 1. Yes, and switch to BYPASS PERMISSIONS` still answer 0, because the branch requires the literal `Try "`. The residual, stated rather than hidden: a human whose own typed text begins `Try "` would read as an empty composer. A capture carries no styling, so the dim hint and typed text are indistinguishable; the alternative is the bug above, which fires on every fresh session rather than on a coincidence.

It happens to be the same string as ready.tmux_pattern for this adapter; it is declared separately anyway, because codex proves the two are not the same question.

bootstrap_message: Read {{bootstrap_file}} and follow it exactly. Reply with the single word READY once you have read it and every skill it lists.
notes: Models: fable, opus, sonnet, haiku, or a full model id. Memory is keyed by working directory, so an agent given its own cwd gets its own memory and keeps it across spawns; --add-dir grants tool access to the repo it actually works in. Set auto_approve: true on the agent to add --dangerously-skip-permissions. Coordinator form verified 2026-09-05: `claude --help` lists `--disallowedTools, --disallowed-tools <tools...>` — 'Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny'. Bash is deliberately NOT denied: the conductor delegates by running ao-topology send/wait/reply, so denying it would break the role. The containment that actually holds for a coordinator is therefore the withheld --add-dir, not this flag. tmux_pattern is the server-side form used by the refresh-client subscription, measured 2026-09-05 against tmux 3.4 on a real Claude input box (`│ > ` matched at its line). It is NOT a translation of `pattern`: tmux searches per line, so `\n` cannot appear; `{`/`}` break the format parser; `:` is the format separator so `[[:space:]]` is unusable; and a trailing `\s` never matches because tmux strips trailing padding. `\s` itself works (glibc extends POSIX ERE). TM-111: the ready pattern requires the prompt glyph to be the last thing on its line, because the folder-trust modal draws "❯ No, exit" and the old pattern matched it — the launcher reported ready, then typed the bootstrap pointer into a modal whose Enter means "No, exit". Measured 2026-09-06 against tmux 3.4 on two live panes: the real input box is "❯" followed by U+00A0 and nothing else, which #{C/r:^\s*[│|]?\s*[>❯][^a-zA-Z0-9]*$} matches at its line, while the modal's menu row does not match it at all.

attention_patterns.pattern: Is this a project you created or one you trust
attention_patterns.message: Claude is waiting on its folder-trust question for this directory — nobody can answer it from here. Answer it once in a normal terminal (cd into the agent's cwd and run `claude`, choose "Yes, I trust this folder"), then launch again.

attention_patterns.pattern: (Select login method|Log in with your Anthropic account|/login to authenticate)
attention_patterns.message: Claude is showing its login screen and cannot start unattended. Run `claude` once in a normal terminal and sign in, then launch again.
